I'm not familiar with Tutanota. How does it stand in comparison with other popular email services or with a more protected email service like Lavabit before it shut down?
Did you happen to have a Lavabit account? How did the shutdown work? Did you get a chance to get your stuff out of there before they closed?
Unfortunately, I didn't know about Lavabit until the news broke that the owner was taking it down rather than let the government compromise it.

I had an account, let me chime in. No one, or at least no regular customer, was informed beforehand by lavabit and we had no time to backup our mail. Which makes sense, because the entire point of shutting the service down was to find a way around the NSL they received and telling users about anything was most likely prohibited. For the longest time Ladar Levinson could not legally tell anyone why exactly he shut down the service, not even his lawyer; so we - the users - simply got cut off from our mail with the service being down.

Then, some time later, I can't remember how long it was, but definitely more than a few weeks, lavabit went online for a very brief period allowing people to retrieve their mail. To me this looked like a honey pot but as far as I know there were no official statements except that it was an opportunity for users to get their mail archive. I did not take any chances at the time, mostly because I had local copies of my mail anyway.

I hold no grudge towards Ladar Levinson, in my eyes he was facing a tough situation and chose to keep his promise rather than fold to preassure. Today he is developing a new protocol to replace E-Mail in cooperation with Silent Circle, you can check out all details about protocol and implementation here.

As long as we are using E-Mails though, I would recommend having offline copies of all your mail via [1], send mails from a local mail client that supports GPG [2] and encrypt them before they leave your network.

tutamail is trying to do that without the hassle of setting up GPG, but then you have to trust javascript crypto and the scripts their server is serving.

[1] http://offlineimap.org/

[2] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GNU_Privacy_Guard#Application_support (I recommend Thunderbird+Enigmail for beginners and sup for terminal enthusiasts)
